\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Definitions}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Randomization.Definitions
\section{Overview}
Independent Walsh signs randomize the orthogonal components of a finite-product function. Coordinate noise, anisotropic noise, and pointwise notable-coordinate families describe related spectral operations.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Randomized orthogonal expansion]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.randomization}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.component, BooleanAnalysis.chiS}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, $r\in\{0,1\}^n$, and $x\in\Omega$. Define $R_rf(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}\chi_S(r)f_S(x)$, where $f_S$ is the orthogonal component and $\chi_S(r)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{r_i}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Randomization moment norm]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.randomizationNorm}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.randomization, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $q\in\mathbb R$, and $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. For $R_rf(x)=\sum_S\chi_S(r)f_S(x)$ and uniform independent $r\in\{0,1\}^n$, define $\|Rf\|_q=(\mathbb E_{x\sim P}\mathbb E_r|R_rf(x)|^q)^{1/q}$ using real powers.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Noise in one coordinate]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.coordinateNoise}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.laplacian}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, a coordinate $i$, $\rho\in\mathbb R$, and $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Define $N_{i,\rho}f=f-L_if+\rho L_if$, where $L_i$ subtracts the conditional expectation over coordinate $i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Anisotropic product noise]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.anisotropicNoise}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.component}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, rates $r_i\in\mathbb R$, and $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Define $T_{\boldsymbol r}f(x)=\sum_S(\prod_{i\in S}r_i)f_S(x)$ using the orthogonal components $f_S$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Pointwise spectral influence]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.localSpectralInfluence}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.component}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, a coordinate $i$, and $x\in\Omega$. Define $\mathcal I_i(f,x)=\sum_{S\ni i}f_S(x)^2$ using the orthogonal components of $f$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Initial notable coordinates]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.notableCoordinates}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.localSpectralInfluence}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, $\tau\in\mathbb R$, and $x\in\Omega$. Define $J_\tau(f,x)=\{i\in[n]:\tau\le\sum_{S\ni i}f_S(x)^2\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Notable subset family]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.notableFamily}
\leanok
For every $J\subseteq[n]$ and $k\in\mathbb R$, define $\mathcal F(J,k)=\{S\subseteq J:|S|\le k\}$, comparing the natural cardinality with the real cutoff.
\end{definition}
